conviction_note: The findings net to about zero: the habitual beat against a guided-down Q2, the 81% rise in short interest since July and the sale optionality on one side; Asian port congestion lasting into October, EMEA and FX on the other. p_up sits at 47 rather than 50 because this name has sold its last two beats (-3.03%, -1.24%), 5 of its 7 recorded prints fell, and the skew pays for downside. abs_move is 10, below the 12.9% event-implied move and well above the 3.03% median, because the print carries an H2 Michael Kors return-to-growth claim and the FY $3.4B/$2.15 guide.
bar: Company Q2 FY27 guide (Aug 5 2026): revenue ~$780M (MK ~$645M, JC ~$135M), operating income ~$10M, diluted EPS ~$0.20; FY27 revenue ~$3.4B, op income ~$170M, EPS ~$2.15 (https://www.capriholdings.com/news/news-details/2026/Capri-Holdings-Limited-Announces-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027-Results/default.aspx). Consensus sits on the guide: EPS $0.21 (Chartmill per search snippet, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CPRI/estimates) and EPS $0.2098 / revenue $786.55M (https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/10/28/capri-cpri-projected-to-announce-earnings-on-friday.html, 2026-10-28, auto-generated site). Two agreeing estimate sources plus a company guide, so the bar is sourced. Note the Q2 guide was ~8% below the $851M consensus that stood before Aug 5.
positioning_check: Short interest 14,314,698 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 4.48 days to cover, ~12.6% of the 113.65M shares outstanding. That is up from 7,900,089 on 2026-07-31 (+81%) and from 11.4M on 08-31; it has held ~14.2-14.5M since 09-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/cpri/shortinterest, FINRA data). Moderately crowded short, built after the Aug guide cut. BlackRock 13G/A: 16.78M shares, 14.8%, event date 2026-09-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1530721/000201238326003951/primary_doc.xml). Options (baseline): 25d skew +6.01 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.45 (call-heavy open interest), event-implied move 12.89%, ATM IV 72.9%. Run-up: +8.18% over 20d, -4.25% over 5d, 43% below the 52-week high.

findings.finding: Capri has guided low and printed above its own quarterly bar on the last two prints. Q1 FY27 adj EPS was $0.67 against $0.39 consensus, revenue $769M against $757M; Q4 FY26 was $0.22 against $0.12. The Q2 guide of $780M / $0.20, which consensus ($786.6M / $0.21) now matches, embeds two items that are timing rather than demand: ~$50M of Michael Kors inventory held up by Asian port congestion, and ~$10M of wholesale shipments pulled into Q1. The likely Q2 print is therefore modestly above the bar (I put revenue about +1%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has sold beats. Q1 FY27 (2026-08-05) beat EPS by 72% with a revenue beat but cut the FY revenue guide, and the stock fell 3.03%. Q4 FY26 (2026-05-27) beat EPS and fell 1.24%. Q3 FY26 (2026-02-03) fell 13.22%. The only large up move was +14.51% on 2025-08-06.
findings.why_not_priced: If the habitual beat were priced, consensus would sit above the guide (it sits at $0.21 against $0.20 and $786.6M against $780M) and the stock would have run into the print. Instead it is -4.25% over 5 days, with the skew paying for downside. What is not priced is how big the beat is. The reaction function caps the size of this finding.
findings.independence: Q2 guide composition (the $50M inventory delay and the $10M wholesale timing shift) is from the company release: https://www.capriholdings.com/news/news-details/2026/Capri-Holdings-Limited-Announces-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027-Results/default.aspx. The same document family as the bar, so this is one finding, not two.

findings.finding: The Asian port congestion that Capri blamed for ~$50M of lost Q2 Michael Kors revenue (called 'temporary' on Aug 5) had not cleared by October. Dimerco's October 2026 Asia-Pac freight report (published ~Oct 1) says Shanghai would stay heavily congested into mid-to-late October with berthing waits above 5 days, Yantian was under intake limits, and Asia-US ocean rates were rising on blank sailings to near-pandemic levels, pushing cargo to air. That puts Q3 holiday inventory flow and freight cost at risk, and with them the H2 Michael Kors return to growth that the FY $3.4B guide rests on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 5 2026 FY revenue cut (from $3.525B to $3.4B, partly on these same inventory delays) drew -3.03% despite a large EPS beat. In Feb 2026 a guidance/trend disappointment drew -13.22%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus FY revenue still sits at about the $3.4B guide, and the Q2 guide treated the congestion as a one-quarter timing item. If the market expected it to persist into Q3, FY estimates would be below guide, which no source shows. The 6-vol-point put skew may partly carry it.
findings.independence: Proxy: freight-forwarder data, not a Capri statement on Q3. The company's own attribution to Asian port congestion is in https://english.aawsat.com/fashion/5303799-capri-cuts-revenue-outlook-iran-war-hits-michael-kors-sales (2026-08-05). The same Dimerco content is covered by https://www.sdcexec.com/transportation/trucking/news/22975771/dimerco-peak-season-extended-asia-freight-demand-exceeds-forecasts (one underlying report).

findings.finding: Short interest nearly doubled into the print: 7.9M shares on 2026-07-31, 14.3M on 2026-10-15 (~12.6% of shares outstanding, 4.48 days to cover). On top of that, WWD reported in late September that Capri has informally approached potential acquirers. That combination puts a squeeze and takeover-optionality floor under any print that does not cut the FY guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print with this short build. The +14.51% move on 2025-08-06 is the name's one large upside reaction, and it came off a depressed base.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is not a fact the market misses. It is the asymmetry: shorts at 4.5 days to cover pay more on a relief print than longs lose on a disappointment. The call-heavy open interest (put/call 0.45) agrees with this; the put skew does not.
findings.independence: Sale exploration: https://fashionunited.com/news/business/is-capri-holdings-up-for-sale/2026092574852 (late Sept 2026, citing WWD; informal, a near-term deal unlikely).

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Capri's Aug 5 guide show European and Middle East demand weaker in Jul-Sep. Moncler's Q3 EMEA was -8% on weaker domestic demand and fewer tourists. Hermès grew in every region except the Middle East. LVMH's CFO called the Middle East still a headwind. Capri guided only ~$15M of softer EMEA in Q2 ($50M for the FY). Michael Kors EMEA was $142M in Q1 (-5.3%) and Jimmy Choo EMEA $82M, so a further low-single-digit EMEA shortfall is ~$5-10M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EMEA softness was one of three reasons for the Aug 5 FY revenue cut (-3.03% reaction). No separate history on this line.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (Moncler Q3 to 30 Sept 2026; exact publication day not shown)
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue sits at or slightly above the guide ($786.6M against $780M). If the peer EMEA weakness had been pushed through, estimates would sit below the guide.
findings.independence: Hermès Q3 2026: every region grew except the Middle East, https://www.pursebop.com/hermes-holds-the-reins-in-q3-2026-as-leather-goods-lead/. Peer proxy only; Capri has not commented since Aug 5.

findings.finding: US luxury demand held up in Jul-Sep at the peers that have reported. Prada's Americas grew +5% organic in Q3 (the strongest region). Kering said North America was Gucci's most resilient market, with Kering NA up 2%. LVMH said the US was still growing. Michael Kors Americas is ~63% of MK revenue ($372M in Q1, -9.9%), so this is a modest support for the Q2 Americas line. Net of the rest: the Q1 Americas decline was brand-specific (fewer promotions, less off-price), so peer strength transmits only weakly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MK Americas fell 9.9% in Q1 FY27 and the stock fell 3.03%. No print in the baseline shows a positive reaction to an Americas beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is high-end luxury read across to an accessible-luxury brand, which is why the size is small. Tapestry, the closest US comparable, does not report until Nov 5, so the market has no direct US accessible-luxury read yet.
findings.independence: Kering Q3 2026, NA most resilient for Gucci: https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/kering-q3-revenue-remains-stable-as-jewelry-and-eyewear-offset-gucci-contraction/2026102391016 (2026-10-23). LVMH Q3: https://fashionunited.com/news/business/lvmh-q3-organic-revenue-growth-slows-amid-china-downturn/2026101375147 (2026-10-13).

findings.finding: The euro weakened after Capri set its 'updated foreign currency exchange rate assumptions' on Aug 5. EUR/USD month-end was 1.1596 in August and 1.1355 in September (-2.1%, Banque de France). That adds a small revenue headwind to the H2 portion of the $3.4B FY guide, which already carries $35M of FX.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX was one of the reasons for the Aug 5 FY revenue cut (-3.03%).
findings.why_not_priced: FX is public and estimates usually absorb it, so most of this is priced. What remains is whether Capri trims the FY revenue line again for it on the call.
findings.independence: none (single series; macro-to-company transmission, unconfirmed by Capri).

findings.finding: Capri hired Catherine So, Tiffany's General Counsel through the LVMH-Tiffany deal era, as Chief Legal & Sustainability Officer, effective 2026-10-19 (8-K Sept 16; Form 3 filed Oct 28). The hire came in the weeks WWD reported informal sale approaches. The Q2 call is management's first public appearance since that report, and any comment on strategic alternatives lands in the window. Against a deal: the 10-Q makes a change of control an event of default under the credit agreement and carries an $809M net-investment-hedge liability.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Dec 2024 WWD report that Capri was exploring a sale of Versace and Jimmy Choo drew up to +7% premarket (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/capri-holdings-exploring-sale-of-versace-jimmy-choo-wwd-reports). There is no print reaction on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the sale report is public. The size covers only the chance that management says something on the call. Capri declined to comment on 'rumors or speculation', so 'no comment' is the base case.
findings.independence: Form 3, So Catherine Wen Hwa, officer, period 2026-10-19: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1530721/000095014226002873/es260847294_3-so.xml. Change-of-control default and hedge terms: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001530721/000153072126000081/cpri-20260627.htm

findings.finding: IEEPA tariff refund: Capri booked a $65M receivable in FY26 ($40M through COGS, $25M through inventory), collected $6M in Q1, and collected another $43M after quarter-end, $49M by 2026-07-31 (10-Q subsequent events). The Q2 cash flow and net debt will show it, but nothing new reaches the P&L.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The refund was first recognised in Q4 FY26 (2026-05-27, -1.24%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: disclosed in the 10-Q and already in the receivable. Filed for completeness at zero, as cash that supports the buyback ($871M authorisation remaining) and net debt ($224M at Q1).

findings.finding: BlackRock reported 16.78M shares (14.8%) as of 2026-09-30 on a 13G/A filed 2026-10-27. That is passive ownership concentration and adds nothing directional.
findings.why_not_priced: Public filing; no directional content. Filed so the panel sees it.

baseline_tension: The evidence is mixed. The beat history, the 81% short build and the sale optionality cut against the 6-vol-point put skew. Port congestion, EMEA and FX agree with it. The skew and this name's habit of selling beats keep p_up just under 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction; this name sells beats): beat-history finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6.
Lesson 7 (a negative against crowded short interest): port-congestion finding cut from -1.0 to -0.8 because short interest is 12.6% with 4.5 days to cover.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): IEEPA refund cut from +0.1 to 0.0; it is cash only, already in the receivable, with no P&L path.

Lessons 5 and 9 left the peer proxies (EMEA -0.5, Americas +0.3, FX -0.3) as small and separately filed; nothing else changed. p_up stays at 47 because the reaction history and the skew offset the lean toward 50.
